requirement_text.REQ-072: Port src/api/tenant_context.zig (104 lines) and src/api/trace_context.zig (55) as the per-request context every tenant-scoped handler reads, and build the single shared mechanism that turns a cross-tenant access into an indistinguishable 404. This requirement exists so INV-5 is discharged once, structurally, instead of being re-implemented and re-tested in each of the fifteen route requirements that follow. IDIOM TRANSLATION, mandatory: trace_context.zig and pipeline_context.zig (45) use Zig threadlocal storage for the per-request correlation id -- carry the trace id explicitly on conn.assigns (mirrored into Logger.metadata/1 for log correlation only), do NOT port a process-dictionary or ETS global standing in for a thread-local. pipeline_context.zig itself has no separate Letflow module: its content folds into this one, stated in the moduledoc rather than silently dropped. THE SCOPING MECHANISM (load-bearing half): one function derives the Ecto :prefix from conn.assigns[:auth_context][:tenant_id] via Letflow.TenantProvisioning.schema_name_for_tenant/1 (REQ-022's existing mechanism, per decision 0003 Dimension B and decision 0006, which removed tenant_id from schema-isolated tables entirely -- so the Postgres schema IS the only scoping these rows have). Handlers obtain their prefix ONLY from this function; no handler constructs a schema name itself or accepts a tenant identifier from the request path, query string, body, or a header. Because the prefix comes from the authenticated token rather than the request, a lookup for another tenant's resource simply finds nothing in the caller's schema -- making the 404 identical to a never-existed 404 by construction, with no separate existence check to leak timing. SECURITY (INV-1, INV-5, INV-6): this module is where all three are discharged for the whole stage.

Full WF-02 pipeline warranted: Step 1 design -> 1b gate -> 2a implement -> 2c security gate (in scope, this is the tenant-scoping mechanism itself) -> 2d idiom/decision-record gate -> 3 test design -> 3b gate -> 4 test run -> 5 release validation -> 6 doc update -> Step Final merge.

Key design constraint to carry into Step 1: no handler may construct a schema name itself or accept a tenant identifier from the request path/query/body/header -- the scoping function's only input is conn.assigns[:auth_context][:tenant_id], already resolved by REQ-071's AuthPipeline. The cross-tenant 404 property must be demonstrated by BYTE-IDENTICAL responses (same status, same body) between a real cross-tenant access and a never-existed-id access, AND by equal query counts between the two paths (no early-exit timing signal) -- both are explicit acceptance criteria, not implementation details to infer.

Complete the handoff: set status COMPLETED, fill result.git_evidence with branch_name and push_status, set next_action to 'Route to CODE-DESIGNER (Step 1)'.
